Safeguarding
The staff at Abbey Wood Nursery School are committed to working in partnership with parents and carers to ensure the wellbeing of your child.
The welfare of your child is our first priority and we will do our best to ensure they feel safe and secure.
We have a legal obligation to monitor and report any:
When your child starts with us you are accepting this legal obligation.
We value our partnership with families and recognise the importance of honest and open communication. In the majority of cases, if we had any concerns we would discuss them with you. It is extremely rare that a concern would not be discussed with you and would most likely occur in a crisis situation, if it was in the best interests of your child’s safety.
Unexplained or non-accidental injuries
Confidentiality
Our staff recognise the diverse circumstances and experiences of the families in our community and are very sensitive and thoughtful about any information that you share. They can not and will not keep information confidential if it concerns the safety or welfare of children or the adults that look after those children, if they believe they are at risk of harm. In this case they would pass on information to the school’s Designated Safeguarding Team.
Responsibility
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility. When we talk and listen to a child we help them to have a voice. Having a voice that is heard is the most powerful safeguarding tool a child can have. At Abbey Wood Nursery School we want all of our children to be confident enough to make choices. Having freedom to make choices also means the child has the freedom to say ‘No!’ or ‘Stop! I don’t like it!’.
If you have any concerns about keeping children safe or any questions about our safeguarding policy and procedures, please see a member of our Designated Safeguarding Team.

pageCache.text:
Forest School at Abbey Wood Nursery School
The history of Forest Schools
Forest School originated in Denmark in the early 1980’s. They found that children who had participated in outdoor learning were arriving at school with strong social skills, ability to work both as part of a group and
individually and generally had high self-esteem and confidence.
Forest Schools was introduced in the UK during the 1990’s and Greenwich was the first borough in London to participate.
What will my child do in Forest School?
Sessions will run for approximately 1 to 1 and half hours. Every session will start and finish at base camp. Children will be reminded of the rules at the beginning of each session after which they will be introduced to the activity and any new equipment. Children will then choose to either take part in the activity or to revisit a previous task. Equally they may choose to explore and investigate the woodland area.
Many of the tasks set will involve natural materials within the woodland area and may involve your child become messy.
All children are provided with waterproof clothing and wellies so if they get wet or dirty it will not be an obstacle for your child’s learning.
What are the benefits of Forest Schools?
Recent studies have shown that children who participate in Forest School sessions grow in confidence and self-esteem. They develop a variety of life skills including, independence, communication and self-discovery.
Forest Schools will stimulate your child’s imagination, creativity and increase their knowledge in the world around them.
‘Imagine jumping in puddles, hide and seek, building shelters and much, much more’.
‘Every child should experience Forest Schools’
Where is Forest School Located?
Our forest school is on site, located at the back of the school. This is a purpose built safe space that our forest school leads can take the children to and learn about the environment, plants, trees, mini breasts and the world around them.

Applying for a Primary School Place
If your child is due to start primary school in September 2026, you need to apply for a primary school place. The deadline for applications is 15 January 2026.
If you miss the closing date, you'll still need to apply online.

Before you apply
You can apply for up to six primary schools, listing them in order of preference.
Consider each school's admissions policies and previous years' application rates to see whether your child is likely to be offered a place.
For an indication of addresses offered by each school in the previous admission, check the RBG primary school offers map.
Your preference schools can be in Royal Greenwich or in other areas, but they cannot be independent (fee paying) schools.
You do not have to list six schools, but the more schools you list, the better your chances of being offered a place at one of them.
Tips on using your preferences wisely
Your preferences are up to you, but do be realistic. There's no guarantee you'll be offered a place at a preference school but here are some recommendations:
Apply online
The easiest way to apply is through the eAdmissions portal – it's quick, easy and secure - and it's the fastest way to hear the results.
Please make sure that you rank your preferences in the order you genuinely want them to be considered. Any changes you wish to make to your preferences after the closing date will only be considered when all applications, including those submitted late, have been processed.

E-Safety
Young children are using technology more and more. This can be a phone, tablet, laptop or watching programmes. A recent report found that some 45% of 3- to 4-year-olds use YouTube, and 52% of 3- to 4-year-olds go online for an average of almost nine hours per week. It is important that young children know the importance of staying safe online and how to use technology in a safe way.
Online safety is a safeguarding issue. We all need to keep children safe in the “real world” and the “digital world”. Schools now mainly communicate with parents online vie email or school apps and a growing number of children have access to the internet at home. It is important parents are aware of the benefits and risks associated with internet use and how to support their children.
Internet matters have produced a leaflet online safety tips for parent 0-5.

You can also find helpful videos on their site on how to limit screen time and set up restrictions on your child’s devices.

School Meals
Lunch and Snacks at Abbey Wood Nursery School
Lunch and snack times are very important here at the nursery and we encourage snack times to also be a time to sit and socialise with our friends.
Snacks: In each class we have an area available serving healthy snacks and water – in the morning and in the afternoon. The children are notified that snacks are available and can make the choice if they would like to join the table for a light snack, after washing their hands. Children are offered snacks, that consist of cereals, toast, fruit and other healthy snacks. This is funded through the half termly snack donation contributions.
Lunch: We are really lucky to have our own kitchen on site. Tracey prepares delicious, nutritionally balanced meals each day. The children eat in small groups at tables with tablecloths and a personalised place setting in their classes and are served by the class staff – an adult sits at each table with them. This is encouraged to be a relaxing enjoyable time, where children can receive a hot nutritious meal. We feel this is an important element of the day where children continue to develop, learn about different foods, likes and dislikes and how to use cutlery with increasing skills and autonomy.
Changes within Early Years education have resulted in the introduction of Packed Lunches. However we have strict guildelines that need to be followed to ensure your child has a nutritious and acceptable lunch experience . These guidelines can be found at the following link: Lunch time guildelines.pdf
Our Lunch menus: Daily lunch charges (£2.80 per meal from September 2025) to be paid through the child’s ParentPay account.
There is always a vegetarian option available
We are happy to meet any particular dietary needs for your child for medical, lifestyle or religious reasons.
We ask that a week’s lunch money (£14.00 per week) be paid in advance, via ParentPay. (Please ask one of the office team, if you would like to know more).
Families on Income Support or Job Seekers Allowance might be eligible for free school meals. Please ask in the office for more information and a copy of the FSM application form. Alternatively, click link below to download a FSM form, once completed return form to the school office.

Enrichment at Abbey Wood Nursery School
We offer a wide range of additional experiences to inspire, challenge, and support our children. Because every child is an individual, our enrichment activities adapt to meet their changing needs.
Here is a look at the exciting adventures we shared during the 2025–26 academic year.
🌳 On-Site Forest School
We are incredibly fortunate to have our own dedicated Forest School right here on the Abbey Wood Nursery School grounds. Children enjoy outdoor learning without ever needing to leave our safe environment. Our certified Forest School Leader plans engaging, hands-on outdoor sessions that build confidence, resilience, and a deep connection to nature. (Discover more on our dedicated Forest School page).
🎭 Cultural & City Adventures
We love taking learning beyond the classroom to give children memorable real-world experiences:
The Unicorn Theatre: Our older children took an exciting train journey into central London for an immersive theatre performance of the three little pigs. For many, the train ride itself was a thrilling new milestone.
The National Maritime Museum: A fun-filled day out exploring local maritime history and interactive exhibits using public transport.
Woodlands Farm: A hands-on visit via public transport where the children met, learned about, and interacted with live animals.
Inclusive Community Visits
London Museum Docklands: This fully accessible venue wais a highlight of our calendar. As the museum is so inclusive we invited parents of children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) to join us on this trip. It offers families a safe, fully supported day out alongside staff who understand their children's unique needs, providing all those that attended real-world strategies for community outings.
🎨 Community & Creativity
The Community Mural: Our children collaborated with the University of the Third Age, our local care home, the local community and families during Stay & Play sessions to create a beautiful community mural. We were honoured to welcome the Mayor of Greenwich, Councillor Linda Bird, to the Nursery School for the official unveiling.
Our Nursery Library: We celebrated the grand opening of our brand-new library space, sparking a lifelong love for reading and storytelling.
🎈 Special Events & Celebrations
Sir David Attenborough’s 100th Birthday: A whole day dedicated to nature in honour of his centenary milestone! The children built bug hotels, constructed their own binoculars, and went on exciting bug hunts.
July Family Box Adventure: We are currently planning a grand summer adventure focusing entirely on open-ended creativity with cardboard boxes!
🌱Learning About Life Cycles
Our Nursery Fish Tank: The children love observing our resident fish and learning how to care for them. This hands-on experience teaches them about aquatic environments, responsibility, and daily animal care routines.
Living Eggs Project: Every year, we welcome ten eggs to the nursery and eagerly watch them hatch into fluffy chicks. Families love joining us for our special Saturday Chick Stay & Play a beloved tradition where our leavers can return to hold the chicks!
Raising Butterflies: In the summer term, each classroom receives packs of chrysalides. The children get to experience and watch them transform into beautiful butterflies up close before setting them free.

Curriculum
Curriculum Rationale
At Abbey Wood Nursey School we have designed a broad and balanced curriculum with the intent that all children will master the skills they need to secure a strong foundation in early learning.
The curriculum enables staff to explore the broad interests that children of a particular age may have, but also allows space for staff to create activities and learning opportunities for children around individual interests, such as cooking or dressmaking. By using the child as the starting point, we are able to radiate out and explore how the school and the family can support the child, and what the child is able to contribute to the community. This holistic view of the child enables support to be individually targeted.
Surrounding the child is the school community and family. Staff are able to acknowledge and explore big ideas that impact the children’s families, through learning about heritage and encourage children to see their role in these events. At the same time, staff recognise that individual family changes may have an impact on a child, for example a new sibling. We have space in our curriculum to address these changes and develop emotional resilience and language to discuss what’s happening.
We recognise the role that the school has in supporting children to begin to make sense of the world. The school has educated generations of families and the community has diversified over the 80 years the school has been open. The school is at the centre of the community and we want children to see and experience that, and learn from it. We also want children to begin to explore big events in the world to help them feel a sense of belonging – laying the foundations for the move to Reception. We explore the impact of Black History Month and events like Children in Need so that the children feel a sense of belonging to a community wider than Abbey Wood.

My children needed time to trust others and unknowingly I needed that that time to trust others to be able to let go! Without pushing my children have just flourished in your care, and are so happy, confident and beyond able. It in turn helped them bloom in every aspect of their life beyond your nursery and for that I honestly can’t ever thank you enough. Me and A are gutted he has to leave so soon but we are very excited to see C grow with you for another year."

Whenever I come to collect C – and to enjoy his sports day! The nursery seems such a happy place with contented children and caring and supportive staff and I am really impressed.
